paper.abstract_en: Quantum key distribution (QKD) has emerged as a promising technique for secure communication in the post-quantum era, offering information-theoretic security against eavesdroppers with unlimited computational power. While fiber-based and satellite QKD systems have demonstrated impressive distances and key rates, terrestrial free-space QKD, which shows potential for secure mobile and wireless payment applications, remains relatively under-investigated due to severe ambient light interference. Here, we present a QKD link operating in the ultraviolet-C (UV-C) region, which is, to the best of our knowledge, the first such example. This has the potential to leverage the “solar-blind” nature of the UV-C region and mitigate sunlight interference. By integrating high-speed AlGaN micro-LEDs with silicon photomultiplier (SiPM)-based single-photon detectors (SPDs), we achieve a secure key rate (SKR) exceeding 1 Mbit/s. Furthermore, we analyze the system’s robustness to ambient light and propose a strategy for full sunlight rejection. Our results establish UV-C as a promising spectral window for terrestrial free-space QKD, paving the way for QKD implementations in daylight conditions.
